To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
18 out 22 missense variants and 2 novel intronic variants are pathogenic for HHT2.

1) 18 missense ACVRL1 variants are functionally defective; 2) one missense variant induces a splicing defect; 3) one intronic variant is pathogenic due to its splicing defect; and 4) functional and splicing assays are useful tools in the genetic diagnosis of HHT2.
Functional and splicing analyses of novel and known ACVRL1 variants identified a novel mutation (p. Ile245Val) and a previously reported one (c.1047+5G>A) with splicing defect.
